title: When the Regiment Turns
premise: In the aftermath of a brutal border war, Gideon Thornbury has spent fifteen years as a regimental nurse, quietly recording in a hidden ledger the names of soldiers erased from official dispatches—deserters executed without trial, casualties blamed on their own companies, and one officer, Captain Elias Wren, listed as dead at the Battle of Harrow Fen. When a scarred stranger arrives bearing letters in Wren's unmistakable hand, Gideon learns Wren survived, was branded a traitor to cover a colonel's catastrophic order, and is dying in hiding. To clear his name before the victors' historians seal the official record, Gideon must risk everything: the ledger, the found family of orderlies and widows who shelter them, and a slow-burning love neither expected. The book ends with Gideon testifying before a commission of inquiry, ledger in hand—Wren's name restored posthumously after his death mid-trial, and Gideon choosing to stay with the regiment's forgotten rather than vanish into safety.
about_author: Lena Voss is the pen name of a former military archivist who spent a decade cataloguing regimental records and the silences between them. She writes historical fiction about the people history files under 'miscellaneous.'

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Names
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. In a converted farmhouse hospital, Gideon tends the wounded and secretly records names omitted from dispatches, establishing the ledger's rules and the quiet family of orderlies who protect it. When news arrives that the war's official history is being commissioned, fear ripples through the ward. Emotional beat: the cost of invisibility, and the first hint that silence has an expiration date.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Gate
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. A gaunt traveler collapses at the gate carrying letters sealed in handwriting Gideon knows intimately—Captain Elias Wren's, officially dead for fifteen years. The letters speak of Harrow Fen, of an order given and disowned, of a name that must be restored before the historians finish their work. Emotional beat: shock cracking open fifteen years of careful concealment.

chapters.title: What Harrow Fen Buried
chapters.summary: Stranger's POV (Tomas Wren, the captain's brother). Tomas recounts finding his brother alive two years ago: wounded, stripped of rank, hiding under a false name while Colonel Ashcombe's report blamed him for the disaster. He carries Wren's testimony but not enough proof. Emotional beat: grief reframed as betrayal; the weight of inherited shame.

chapters.title: The Widow's Testimony
chapters.summary: POV of Marta, the cook and widow of a Harrow Fen casualty. She recognizes details from Tomas's account that match what her husband wrote in his last letter—evidence the ledgers alone can't provide. The household debates whether to help, knowing Ashcombe now sits on the inquiry board. Emotional beat: found family choosing courage over safety.

chapters.title: Ashcombe's Men
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Soldiers arrive ostensibly to requisition supplies, actually searching for deserters—and asking pointed questions about strangers. Gideon hides Tomas and realizes someone inside the regiment has been reading the official record against them. An old ally warns that the commission convenes in six weeks. Emotional beat: the hunter at the door; time compressing.

chapters.title: Letters Never Sent
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Gideon reads Wren's letters fully and writes back for the first time, confessing fifteen years of recorded names—including how Gideon once falsified a death record to save a boy from execution. The correspondence becomes an intimacy built entirely on paper. Emotional beat: love arriving sideways, through duty's language.

chapters.title: The Journey to Harrow Fen
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Gideon and Tomas travel to the battlefield site to find the surveyor's map proving the artillery order was misfiled—Ashcombe's own signature on the fatal coordinates. They find the map but are spotted by patrols; Tomas takes a bullet covering Gideon's escape. Emotional beat: sacrifice, and proof gained at terrible price.

chapters.title: Where Loyalties Lie
chapters.summary: Marta's POV. Back at the farmhouse, the household fractures—one orderly betrays the ledger's location to protect his son conscripted into Ashcombe's company. The ledger is seized, though Gideon had already copied the crucial pages. Wren, dying, arrives secretly to testify in person. Emotional beat: betrayal and forgiveness within the found family.

chapters.title: The Commission
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Before the inquiry, Ashcombe's counsel dismantles witnesses one by one until Gideon takes the stand, producing the copied pages, the map, and Wren himself—alive, wrecked, and unflinching. Ashcombe attempts to discredit Gideon's falsified death record; instead it exposes the pattern of cover-ups. Wren collapses mid-testimony. Emotional beat: climax—the private ledger made public record.

chapters.title: On the Record
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Wren dies three days after the verdict clears his name; the commission orders the histories amended. Gideon declines a pension and a quiet posting elsewhere, choosing instead to keep the farmhouse hospital, with Tomas and Marta beside them, and adds Wren's name to the ledger in ink, not pencil. Emotional beat: resolution—inheritance redefined as memory kept deliberately, love chosen over erasure.
